On The 4 th Of October, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 43073 of 2024
 Kamal Singh
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri D.S. Rajawat - Advocate for applicant.
 Shri Yogesh Parashar - Public Prosecutor for the State
 Order

This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.150 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Bahadurpur, District - Ashoknagar (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(I), 376(2)(N), 376(3), 376(2)(), 506 of IPC &
Section 3/4 , 5L/6 and 5N/6 of POCSO Act.

The first bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 04.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.29037/2024.
2 .
It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the matter.

It is submitted that after dismissal of first bail application of applicant as withdrawn on 04.09.2024, Prosecutrix 'A', Prosecutrix 'B' and their mother have been examined before the Trial Court and they have turned hostile and have not supported the story of prosecution.
It is further submitted that the DNA NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:17576 2 MCRC-43073-2024 report is also negative and there is no evidence on record against the present applicant.
Applicant is in custody since 23.05.2024.
No further custodial interrogation of applicant is required.
He is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by the Court..
He is permanent resident of District Ashoknagar, therefore, there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with prosecution evidence.
The trial will take time to conclude.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
3. Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection by submitting that there are serious allegations against the applicant.

4. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: 5 . Having heard the rival submissions and taking note of the DNA report and the statements of Prosecutrix 'A', Prosecutrix 'B' and their mother, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant may be granted bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.

In case offence of same nature is repeated, this bail order shall automatically stand cancelled;
v) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and vi) The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
7. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Aman Kamal Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179358146/
